gaps.sentence: Can we ___ a phone call before we leave?
gaps.explanation: make a phone call / make a call is the standard collocation.

gaps.sentence: Smoking can ___ serious harm to your health.
gaps.explanation: do harm to something is the fixed phrase; 'make harm' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to ___ friends when you move to a new city.
gaps.explanation: make friends is the fixed expression for forming friendships.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ great progress since she changed schools.
gaps.explanation: make progress is the collocation; after 'has' the past participle 'made' is needed.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ interest on the money it borrows.
gaps.explanation: pay interest is the standard financial collocation.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.
